Reuse core counter logic from the existing XD Redis counter implementation for the s-c-s module adaptation, only modifying the wrapper and configuration to fit the s-c-s module structure to avoid redundant development.

Use GitHub Actions as the CI platform for both s-c-d and s-c-s-m repositories, standardizing pipeline structure (build, test, code quality checks, artifact publishing) and reusing workflow templates to reduce duplication.

Leverage Spring Boot's existing classloader hierarchy and dependency management features for Boot loader external JAR support, extending classpath scanning logic rather than implementing a custom classloader.

Refactor ModuleLauncher to extend Spring Boot's ApplicationRunner for startup logic, replace custom property handling with Spring Boot externalized configuration, and use Boot's classloader extension points for future CP augmentation.

Reuse existing, well-maintained Apache Hadoop HDFS client libraries compatible with Java 17+ for the PHD port, rather than implementing HDFS client functionality from scratch to reduce effort and improve reliability.

Extend the existing StreamController REST API layer for new stream commands, reusing the existing stream service layer business logic to ensure consistency with existing API design and avoid duplicate business logic.
assumptions: All relevant existing codebases (spring-cloud-data, spring-cloud-stream-modules, StreamController, ModuleLauncher, PHD) are accessible, have up-to-date documentation, and are compatible with Java 17+ as required by Spring Framework 6.0.

The development team has existing proficiency with Spring Boot, Spring Cloud Stream, Spring Shell, Redis, Apache HDFS, and GitHub Actions, so no additional training or learning curve is accounted for in effort estimates.
All required third-party dependencies (Redis client, Hadoop HDFS client, database drivers, etc.) are available, compatible with Java 17+, and have appropriate licenses for use in the project.
Existing unit and integration test suites for all modified components are available and can be extended to cover new functionality, with no need to build test infrastructure from scratch.
Test environments for Redis, HDFS, and CI infrastructure are already provisioned and available for development and testing activities, with no delays expected for environment setup.
No unplanned major architectural refactoring of existing core components is required beyond the scope of the defined user stories.
